# Build: profile-manager (Current profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): a plugin to manage build profiles: view, browse, create, edit, delete, everything. Assigned agent: **Landin' Lenny** (book on his card; if busy and the all-rounder router is on main, whoever is free - record who). Register in the **current** profile (id `profile-manager`) + banner entry. (Profile `current` was just created; if it's missing, create it: `node framework/cli/profiles.mjs create "Current" --id current --select`.)

## Build on what exists - don't duplicate
The console already has the **Build profiles** plugin (`build-profiles`: dialog + settings tab, banner chip, switch/create/rename/remove) over `framework/cli/profiles.mjs` (build-profiles@1) and the builds store. Grow THAT plugin into a full manager page (rename the plugin title to 'Build profiles' manager if needed; keep its id, data and every existing feature).

## Features
- **Browse:** framework grid of every profile (collapsible rows): name, id, active star, description, counts (builds running / pending / complete / archived, pending items, queue steps), cost spent + cost left, last activity, created; sort/search/filter. Expand a row: its builds (with agent avatars once crew-live lands), pending list, queue, plan summary, files (`profiles.mjs where`).
- **View** a profile page: all its builds and steps, timeline, totals, links to Builds page views filtered to it.
- **Create** (name, id, description, copy from another profile, catalog on/off, make active), **Edit** (name, description, catalog, colour/icon for the banner chip), **Switch** (one tap; banner chip + context menu), **Duplicate**, **Merge** two profiles, **Move builds** between profiles (multi-select, drag rows onto a profile), **Archive / hide**, **Delete** = take off the list (data kept, restorable) with confirm; a separate 'Delete data too' that is owner-only and irreversible-confirm. Base profile and active profile can't be deleted.
- **Cleanup helper:** flag archived builds that are actually complete (reconciler) - e.g. angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor - with a one-tap fix.
- Context-menu hooks everywhere: 'Build profiles...' and 'Move to profile' on any build row.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (list, get, create, update, select, duplicate, merge, move-builds, archive, remove, restore) so Amber can manage profiles by voice (reads ALLOW policy, changes veto, data delete confirm).

items.title: Automated Browser plugin (drive, record, edit, schedule)
items.detail: Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice), verbatim: "Make me a plugin that shows a browser that can be driven by the app, give it the ability to be automated and to record automation routines through the browser, like make it record in real time what you do and save the events, so you can redo everything that you just recorded, and have a powerful editor to see what each step is doing. Make it so that you can create workflows through the automated browser and record the steps, or do them automatically and record as you go, or record manually, and full powerful editing, able to tweak the JavaScript and whatever you gotta do to make it follow a routine, like go to a site and log in, or go to a site and go to a products page and grab something, and then have a scheduler built into it that you can schedule when to perform these routines." items.title: Merge queue: test once, never twice
items.detail: Stacked merge queue in auto-land (GitHub's native merge queue needs an org-owned repo; MossesX is a personal account). Each ready PR is tested once on top of main + every PR ahead of it on a queue/pr-<n> branch; green head merges with no retest; red is kicked out with a plain reason and the ones behind are rebuilt without it. CI path filters (framework/cli/ci-scope.mjs), light checks on PRs while the queue is on, main push skips jobs the queue already ran on the same code. Merge queue view + banner chip + REST/MCP/CLI (mergequeue_list/add/remove/move). UI Review gate kept.

Make a plugin with a widget that lists the active Claude accounts only. The ones that actually have a human involved, either this one or the helper. It needs to list any account that's actively being run, any session being run by a human, and then you can click a button and you can watch its output live, including voice. It will be able to hear you talking to me, and me talking to you.

Asked whether the person on a watched session should know: "You can have it: 'you're being watched'."

## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
Actually, make it list all sessions, but note whether it's a human or a headless. Only allow voice monitoring of the human.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
In the session list, it needs to list the sessions in a grid, and it needs to show the agent that's running that session. Every time you open a session, you are prompted with a list of agents to select from: who you are, or who do you want to run this session, and then you pick one of the agents. So when you see the sessions listed and you want to assign jobs to one, you open it as a helper and just see who's running it.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
All human sessions need to be meticulously logged so that in the future they can be browsed. It will open it and you can watch in real time the context window and hear or listen to our conversation, as the whole entire session is played back.

## Addendum 4 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
You can configure where to store recordings in the plugin settings interface. You can choose whether you want to store it on the VPS, or in the repo, or in its own container. If you choose VPS, you can select the container from a dropdown list of containers. Or a repo: you can select from a dropdown list of repos. Or you can even store it locally if you want to and have them all synced.

## Addendum 5 (Brett, Nov 4 2026 (voice))
After the session is done, it needs to compress the audio to remove all the dead space where it's not you talking or me talking. Obviously the dead space needs to stay to maintain its real time, but it needs to cut that data out of the stream.

notes.text: Brett: "Without AI." Select and create build must work with no AI: plain UI that assembles the brief from the selected items directly.

Brett: "So whenever you plan something, it gets a file that writes out what it would prompt AI to say. What it would tell you, but it doesn't say anything until you, unless you add it to a new build." Every plan item has a stored, prewritten prompt file. Brett: "You can view that file through hooks, the theater. The different steps, maybe the context menu. Or you can do multiple selection, make them rebuild and view the prompt that it generates. Without AI." The prompt file can be viewed per step (theater/hover view, context menu). Multi-select, then rebuild or preview the generated prompt before sending. All of it without AI.

Brett: progress tracking applies to ALL builds, not only ones started from the planner (builds already split into steps). Every build_start brief includes the check-off instruction, and the console reads the progress live for every build. Resume from the first unchecked step.

Re-added (lost in an overwrite): (a) AmberX task and checklist rows: click a row to see the text discussed; expandable rows show amendments; send a row straight to its own new build. (b) A build from the planner auto-ticks items as it finishes them; the brief lists the item IDs and tells it to tick them. (c) The console tracks progress live without AI, through the console API or a progress file in the build dir; no stopping or resending context; if a build dies, the next run resumes at the first unchecked item.

CORRECTION from Brett: the build manager already tracks build progress, so drop the console-tracking and progress-file notes above. NEW: every build (anything Amber or anyone starts) automatically creates a plan in Plan Studio and goes into a build registry. That plan uses the same steps the build manager will use, so they stay in sync (one source of truth) and tick off together, along with the linked AmberX checklist rows. Registry and planner are categorized by app, plugin, edit, feature, in collapsible trees with sorting and filters.
Brett: the build manager and the planner both read and write progress in the SAME registry, one source of truth, with no separate copies to sync.

# today: approve/deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub."

## Problem
When an axHub approval (confirm or veto countdown) is waiting, the console pops it up (approvals-banner / approval popup), but tapping it navigates to https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>. Brett wants to stay in the console.

## Build
1. In the console's approval popup/banner (and any approval row in the console, incl. phone layout), tapping the approval opens an in-console approval view: title, description, the exact call/command, countdown if veto, and Approve / Deny buttons.
2. Approve / Deny call axHub's approval API server-side from the console (console proxy using its existing axHub auth), never by sending Brett to the axHub site. Show the result in place (approved, denied, ran, failed).
3. No link to the axHub page as the default tap. At most a small secondary "open in axHub" option.
4. Register console actions (e.g. approvals.approve / approvals.deny with id) so they work through console commands too, and make console_show approval:<id> open this in-console view.
5. AmberX phone notifications for approvals should open the console's in-console view, not axHub.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for approve/deny from the console. Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

# Build: Headless progress file + lean CLAUDE.md chain
Orchestrator build id: headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain (planner.builds). Follow the CLAUDE.md chain and rules as usual.

Goal: headless sessions never stop to update the console; they write progress to a small file the console reads. Cut tokens spent on the CLAUDE.md chain.

Steps (each ~10 min, commit after each):
1. Define progress file format + location per build (current step, status, last update, notes).
2. Headless runner (deploy/claude-headless.sh etc.): write/update progress file after each step without pausing. Use it yourself in this build from step 2 on.
3. Orchestrator: include progress file in every new build on registration.
4. Console: read progress file on demand and show where the build is.
5. Remove old stop-to-update-console behavior from headless sessions.
6. Audit the CLAUDE.md chain headless sessions load (files, size, tokens per step).
7. Headless: load a slim build brief instead of full chain; pull rules files only when a step needs them.
8. Load chain once per session, not every step; verify.

Tick each step done in the orchestrator as you go. Finish with README/help update, report, PR to merge queue.

origin.brief:
# claude-accounts-edit: Edit button per account that reruns the wizard

(r2: r1 died at launch, account-2 OAuth expired.)

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "Where it lists the accounts, I need to have an edit button next to the switch buttons... that runs the wizard again."

## Problem
In the console's Claude accounts list (ai-keys "Manage Claude accounts" view and the claude-accounts screen), each account row only has Switch. When an account's login expires, there is no way to re-log that specific account. The add-account wizard only adds a new one. Also: the wizard's "Save current account" fails with a bare 'VPS command failed, exit 1' when nobody is logged in (claude-account save prints 'nothing to save: log in or pass a token'); show that message in the UI.

## Build
1. Add an **Edit** button on every account row, right next to Switch, in every place the account list is shown.
2. Edit opens the existing add-account wizard bound to that account (pre-filled name/slot). Finishing it replaces that account's login/credentials in place: same slot, no new account. Per-build login copies for that account pick up the new credentials.
3. Show a clear state on rows whose login is expired/invalid (e.g. "Login expired").
4. Wizard: surface the claude-account command's own output on failure instead of only 'exit 1'.
5. Register a console action claude-accounts.edit (account id arg) so it runs through console commands too.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for the edit path (re-log replaces creds in place, no duplicate). Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

origin.said:
# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

origin.brief:
# Model UPGRADES need Brett's approval; downgrades don't (Urgent, Opus)

Replaces the stopped build model-switch-approval (folder /root/axf-builds/model-switch-approval, ignore any work there).

Brett Nov 3 2026 (voice), angry: a headless build (agent-swarm-fable-rebuild, PR #247) approved its own Opus -> Fable phase switch in the orchestrator (`orchestrator.mjs act approve`) because its brief said "do every step". Brett: "It cannot be switching the model without my approval. That's not even a veto. That's an approval." Then: "You can downgrade, but you can't upgrade."

New project rule (add to _claude/rules/RULES.md and the decisions log, dated Nov 3 2026): a build may switch to a LOWER model on its own (downgrade, e.g. Fable -> Opus): allowed, no approval, just recorded. Switching to a HIGHER model (upgrade, e.g. Opus -> Fable) needs Brett's explicit APPROVAL (confirm policy), never a veto countdown and never self-approved by a session, agent, headless build or the orchestrator. Ranking: Fable is above Opus (Brett's call). Put the ranking in model-policy (one ordered list, config not code) so future models slot in. A session that reaches an upgrade stops there and asks.

Enforce it:
1. orchestrator approve/phase logic (orchestrator-core.mjs apply + CLI + console server): a downgrade phase passes by itself (record it); an upgrade phase refuses unless approved by Brett: his own signed-in console click or an axHub approval he approves. Detect non-human sources with the same signals used for 'who asked' on approvals (X-Axhub-Source, AXF headless env, agent env). Record who approved and when.
2. vps.build_start / claude-headless.sh / agent job router: launching or relaunching a build on a higher model than its orchestrator step's model is an upgrade too: refuse or hold for approval the same way.
3. Briefs (orchestrator `brief`, headless guidance, agent jobs): say plainly upgrades need Brett and the session stops and asks; downgrades are fine. Remove any wording that lets a session approve an upgrade.
4. Request path: an axHub approval (confirm policy, not veto) titled with the build, the phase and from -> to model; approving it records the approval in the orchestrator.
5. Audit: list every upgrade approved so far by a non-human source (the store's journal), report in the PR; mark agent-swarm-fable-rebuild's s7 Opus -> Fable as self-approved (not Brett's). Note: xlayout-opus and token-control-opus were Fable -> Opus (downgrades), fine under the new rule.

# Build: orch-live-sync (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now, start to finish.

## Problem
The Build orchestrator on main is stale. `_claude/builds/profiles/*/orchestrator.json` is a read-only export of `_claude/builds/store.json`, regenerated after every store write. Sessions write the store on their own feature branch, so main never sees step progress until (if ever) the branch merges. Branch and PR fields are left blank. Result today: in the Urgent profile, dock-engine (done in open PR #245, branch claude/molly-fable) and token-control (done in open PRs #246 claude/token-control and #250 claude/token-control-opus) still show pending with 0 steps done, and theme-editor has an unmerged branch claude/theme-editor nobody linked. Banners and THREADS are wrong as a result.

Brett's rule: every completed step, no matter how small, must reach the orchestrator and appear on main immediately. The orchestrator must be aware every step of the way so it can update the banners and the threads.

## First (before code)
1. Register this build in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `orch-live-sync`, category Urgent, branch claude/orch-live-sync), with the steps below. Register the in-progress banner entry per the standing session rules.
2. Check the pending build queue per the standing rules.

## Steps
- s1 Live status writes to main: a small module (e.g. framework/cli/builds-live.mjs or inside the store IO) so that every store write that changes build/step status (step done, build status, notes, branch, pr) is committed to main immediately as its own tiny status-only commit (store.json + journal + regenerated exports only), independent of whatever feature branch the session is on. Use a separate worktree or git plumbing on origin/main; fetch, apply, commit, push; on non-fast-forward, refetch and re-apply the journal entry (rebase-retry, bounded); never force-push. Code changes stay on the feature branch/PR as now. Avoid conflicts between parallel sessions (journal-append semantics, per-build records). When the feature branch later merges, resolve.py / union merge must not regress statuses (newer rev wins).
- s2 Branch + PR auto-link: when a session creates/pushes a branch or opens a PR for a build, the build's `branch` and `pr` fields are set and written live (s1). Build status shows built-awaiting-merge when all steps are done but the PR is unmerged; complete when merged.
- s3 Reconciler: on every session start and on a timer (VPS cron or the existing hub scheduler), scan open PRs and claude/* branches on GitHub, match them to builds (branch field, build id in branch name/PR title/body, step ids in commits), mark finished-but-unlisted work, fill missing branch/pr fields, and flag orphans in a report and a banner alert. Write results live (s1).
- s4 Banners + THREADS follow the store: every live status change pushes the banner update and appends a THREADS.md entry (one line per change, union-merge friendly).
- s5 Session-start rule: update the session rules / CLAUDE docs so no session trusts the main export alone; it runs the reconciler and reads the live store first.
- s6 Backfill now using the new tools: Urgent profile -> dock-engine all steps done, branch claude/molly-fable, pr #245; token-control s1-s3 done (pr #246, branch claude/token-control), s4-s14 done (pr #250, branch claude/token-control-opus); urgent-builds is complete and merged (2a057cc4), hide/archive it from the active list; theme-editor: inspect branch claude/theme-editor, mark the steps it actually completed, link the branch, and if all 5 steps are done open a PR for it. Run the reconciler across all five profiles (angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor, urgent) and report what it fixed.
- s7 Tests (store write retry, parallel writes, merge no-regress, reconciler matching), full local CI block, report `_claude/builds/reports/orch-live-sync.md`, THREADS.md, open the PR.

Mark each step done through the store as you finish it (that write itself should go live once s1 exists). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026 voice) — read before finishing
- s8 Per-step branch + PR: every step record gets its own `branch` and `pr` fields (plus `merged`/`mergedAt`), set live when that step's work is pushed / PR'd / merged. A build can span several branches and PRs (e.g. token-control: s1-s3 in #246 claude/token-control, s4-s14 in #250 claude/token-control-opus). Build-level branch/pr stay as a summary (list). Reconciler (s3) matches per step. Migrate existing records with empty values; schema + projections + Steps view column.
- s9 Keep live status commits cheap: status writes are plain scripts/git plumbing, zero model involvement beyond one CLI call per step; add paths-ignore for `_claude/builds/**` and THREADS.md to .github/workflows/deploy.yml (and any other workflow on push to main) so status-only commits never trigger CI/deploy; debounce/batch writes within a few seconds into one commit.

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026 voice: "you fix it, I trust you")
- s10 Resolve every claude-sync hold and stop them piling up. Brett delegated the pick to these rules; apply them yourself, don't ask:
  - `_claude/builds/store.json` + journal: merge per record by `rev`/updatedAt, newest wins, never drop a record from either side. Orchestrator/pending/queue exports: regenerate from the merged store (never pick a side).
  - THREADS.md, STATUS.md, decisions.md, LOG.md, sessions/*, handoff notes: union merge (keep every unique line/entry, dedupe identical ones, keep chronological order, decision numbers kept unique).
  - rules/RULES.md, shared rules/RULES.md, preferences.md, persona.md: if one side is a strict superset take it; otherwise union-merge the rule bullets and list any genuine contradiction (same rule, different wording/meaning) in the report for Brett; keep the newer wording in place meanwhile.
  - Anything else: newer content wins; the other side stays recoverable as a hub version (memory_history).
  - Resolve the holds in /opt/axf and on the hub, then make claude-sync apply these rules automatically on every sync (so headless sessions never leave holds again); only real rule contradictions get held, and those raise a banner alert + THREADS line instead of sitting silently.

# Build: headless-tabs (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now.

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `headless-tabs`, branch claude/headless-tabs) with the steps below + in-progress banner entry, per standing rules. Check the pending queue.
- Builds `orch-live-sync` and `notes-vault` are running in parallel and touch the builds store / claude-sync: never hand-edit store.json, go through the orchestrator CLI. If orch-live-sync's live status writes (framework/cli/builds-live.mjs) are on main by the time you finish a step, use them.

## What Brett wants
1. Every terminal tab in the console's terminal (the Windows Terminal plugin / terminal in the console) runs on a session that never dies, like Mosh/Moshi: it survives disconnects, reloads, phone sleep, and stays current. Browsers can't speak Mosh (UDP), so: every tab is backed by a persistent tmux session on the VPS, attached over the console's websocket/pty bridge with automatic reconnect + resume (scrollback replay on reattach, no lost output). The same tmux sessions must be attachable from Brett's Moshi phone app (document the one-line `mosh`/ssh + `tmux attach -t <name>` command in the help pack and show it in a tab menu item "Open in Moshi" that copies it). Closing a tab detaches, it doesn't kill (explicit "Kill session" with confirm).
2. Every time a headless session starts (deploy/claude-headless.sh, `vps.build_start`, agent swarm jobs, orchestrator-launched builds), the console automatically opens a NEW tab attached to that build's tmux session (axf-<name>). Works for builds started while the console is closed too: on open, tabs for all running headless sessions appear.
3. Tab title bar: the agent running it (agent/persona name from the session's env/brief/swarm roster, e.g. the swarm agent name, else the build name) + model + a real-time cost counter that climbs as it spends. Cost: run claude -p with `--output-format stream-json --verbose` (or tee it alongside the human log) and sum usage per message (input, output, cache read, cache write) x the model's price table (config file, not hard-coded in UI); final value reconciles to the result event's total_cost_usd. Expose cost via a small server route/websocket so the title updates live. Show status dot (working / waiting / done / failed).
4. The tab splits into two panes; split direction vertical or horizontal (toggle in the tab menu + default in Settings, remembered per tab). Pane A = the live session. Pane B = the context chain: as the session reads CLAUDE.md and every file it pulls in (imports/@ references, .claude/rules, _claude/rules/RULES.md, shared rules, instructions, persona, memory, THREADS etc.), show the chain as a tree in the order it happens, and print the rules it picks up ONE AT A TIME, deliberately slower than real time (typewriter/reveal pacing, speed setting, skip-to-end button), so Brett can watch what the agent is learning. Source the chain from the session's actual reads (stream-json tool events for Read, plus the CLAUDE.md load order Claude Code uses); rules = the bullet/heading items of each file.
5. Tokens only, follows the hub look, phone-friendly (on narrow screens the split stacks and becomes swipeable).

## Steps
- s1 Persistent tmux-backed tabs + reconnect/resume in the console terminal; Moshi attach command; detach vs kill.
- s2 Headless launcher emits session-start events (claude-headless.sh + build_start path + swarm/orchestrator launches) with build name, agent, model, tmux session; console auto-opens tabs, and lists running ones on load.
- s3 stream-json capture alongside the human log; cost meter service (price table config) + live route.
- s4 Tab title: agent, model, live cost, status dot.
- s5 Split pane with vertical/horizontal toggle + setting.
- s6 Context chain pane: tree in read order + slow rule-by-rule reveal, speed setting, skip.
- s7 Help pack, tests, check-theme/check-controls, lifecycle, UI Review shots, report `_claude/builds/reports/headless-tabs.md`, THREADS.md, PR.
Mark each step done through the store as you finish it. Android port: log as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - where it goes
Everything in this build goes INTO the console's existing built-in Terminal plugin (Terminal v0.3.0: frameless window, tab strip as title bar, connections, profiles, Windows keys; window engine resize/snap/maximize from refactor-all s17-s23, see `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/windows-terminal.md` and `windows-terminal-fable.md`). Extend that plugin; do NOT create a separate terminal plugin or a second terminal UI. Persistent tmux sessions become the Terminal's session backend / a connection type, auto-opened headless tabs are Terminal tabs, title/cost/status live in its tab strip, the split + context-chain pane are Terminal pane features. Bump the Terminal plugin version and keep every existing feature working.

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - clarification, overrides any ambiguity above
Target = the Terminal PLUGIN produced by the Refactor build `windows-terminal` (the Windows-Terminal-style plugin, v0.3.0, in the console's plugins folder). NOT any terminal hardwired into the console core/shell. If the console core has its own built-in terminal, leave it untouched. All features of this build (persistent tmux/Moshi sessions, auto headless tabs, agent name + live cost + status in the tab strip, vertical/horizontal split, context-chain pane) live inside that plugin. If you already started any of it outside the plugin, move it into the plugin.

## ADDENDUM 3 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - Tooltip mode (add as step s8)

- Check the `land` job type (`node framework/cli/agent-job.mjs list`); if an agent owns landing, you are acting for it this once at Brett's request; book it there if the tooling allows.

## How to land each one
For each branch below, in this order: fetch, merge origin/main into the branch in its worktree (/root/axf-builds/<name> where it exists, else a fresh worktree), resolve, run the repo's local CI block (tsc, vite builds of affected apps, check-theme, check-controls, plugin lifecycle, tests touched), push the branch, then fast-forward/merge to main and push main (never force). Close the PR as merged (or merge it via GitHub API) and update its build in the store (complete, per-step branch/pr/merged/mergedAt).
Conflict rules:
- `_claude/builds/store.json`: merge per record (build, step) by rev/updatedAt, newest wins, never drop a record from either side; then regenerate all exports (`orchestrator.json`, profiles/*/orchestrator.json, pending, queue) from the merged store. Journal `_claude/builds/journal/*.jsonl`: union of lines, dedupe identical, keep chronological order.
- THREADS.md, STATUS.md, decisions.md, LOG.md, notes/sessions/handoffs: union merge. Build reports: keep the branch's version (it's that build's own report) unless main's is newer for the same build.
- Hub-synced copies (changes/*.json, _claude/shared/notes/**, apps/*/_claude/**): identical = fine; differing = newer wins.
- REAL code conflicts: resolve them properly if the intent of both sides is clear (both features must keep working; run the tests). If you can't resolve one safely, skip that branch, leave it pushed, and record exactly why in the report; keep going with the rest.

1. claude/notes-vault (PR #256)

# Build: menu-scroll (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "The application menus need to be scrollable when they reach beyond the screen." Assigned agent: **Janitor Joey** (book on his agent-swarm card; set AXF_AGENT=janitor-joey if supported, else record in report + store note). Register in Urgent (id `menu-scroll`) + banner entry.

## Fix (framework level, so every app and plugin gets it)

# Build: toolbar-tap-confirm (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): every EXISTING and FUTURE toolbar uses the Terminal's Tooltip mode (first tap shows what the button does and arms it lit for 3 s, second tap within 3 s runs it, duration configurable; built in headless-tabs PR #259, s8). The double tap is ONLY on phones / touch. On a computer it stays a normal single click (hover tooltip as usual) - 'it really works on a computer.' Assigned agent: **Landin' Lenny** (book on his card; AXF_AGENT=landin-lenny if supported). Register in Urgent (id `toolbar-tap-confirm`) + banner entry.

## Steps
- s1 Lift Tooltip mode out of the Terminal plugin into the framework toolbar component (web reference + axf.css; Compose twin in PORTING.md unless trivial) as one shared behaviour; the Terminal uses the framework version (no duplicate code left in the plugin).
- s2 Device rule: double-tap confirm only when the input is touch (pointer: coarse / touch events / compact window class on a touch device). Mouse/trackpad/pen-hover = single click + hover tooltip. Decide per interaction (a touchscreen laptop: touch = double tap, mouse = single click).
- s3 Adopt everywhere: every toolbar in the console, every plugin, axHub web, AmberX (Capacitor), Molly, walkthrough-studio, templates/boilerplates, so new apps get it by default. Inventory every toolbar first and list them in the report.
- s4 Future-proof: the framework toolbar has it ON by default; a check (like check-controls) fails CI if any toolbar is built outside the framework toolbar or turns the behaviour off without an explicit, recorded reason. Add the rule to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar uses tap-to-confirm on touch (framework toolbar); single click on desktop.'
- s5 Settings > Appearance (or Interaction): on/off for touch, arm duration (default 3 s); per-toolbar override only via the setting, not code. Destructive buttons keep their own confirm on top.
- s6 Tests (touch vs mouse paths, timeout, second tap on a different button re-arms instead of running), screenshots phone + desktop, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/toolbar-tap-confirm.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): make all of this ONE Toolbars plugin
The framework toolbar becomes a **Toolbars plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall) that owns every toolbar in every app, existing and future. Everything below is part of it.

### Settings
- Plugin settings (Settings > Plugins > Toolbars): global on/off for the touch double-tap tip (default on, phone/touch only), arm duration, defaults for all toolbars (theme, colours, density, icon size, labels on/off, position).
- **Every toolbar carries its OWN settings** (stored per toolbar id, synced via axHub like other settings): theming and colours (tokens/assets only: colour theme, style, background, button style, icon/label size, spacing, rounded/flat, opacity), layout (position, orientation, wrap vs scroll vs overflow menu, show/hide, auto-hide), behaviour (double-tap override for this toolbar, tooltips), and its button list.
- **Context-menu hooks on every toolbar** (right-click / long-press): 'Toolbar settings' (that toolbar's own settings), 'Edit toolbar' (opens the Toolbar editor), 'All toolbars...' (Toolbars plugin page that lists and controls every toolbar in the app). Contributed as runtime context items, so every existing and future toolbar gets them; CI check fails any toolbar without them.

### Toolbar editor
- Opens from the toolbar context menu. Add / remove / reorder / group / separators, edit each button (label, icon, tooltip text, action/hook, colour, visibility by level/role, keyboard shortcut), reset to default, undo/redo, live preview, save as an asset so it's hot-swappable and shareable.

### Drag and drop hooks anywhere
- A **hook** = any actionable thing in the app (menu item, nav item, toolbar button, banner item, 'Go to it' hooks, plugin commands from control@1 / plugin-commands-auto, settings pages, screens). Reuse the control@1 command registry and the pending `context-menu-editor` idea (save the action/destination, not the element).
- Drag any hook from anywhere and drop it on a **drop target**: any toolbar, the navigation menu, the banners, application menus, context menus, Home. Drag a button from one toolbar to another; nav menu -> toolbar and toolbar -> nav menu.
- On drop: a **configure dialog that depends on where it's dropped** (toolbar = new button dialog; nav menu = nav item dialog; banner = banner item dialog; menu = menu item dialog), prefilled with default values from the hook (label, icon, action, tooltip), with all the options for that target. Confirm creates it; move vs copy choice (default: copy from menus, move between toolbars), undo.
- Make it a framework contract: `drop-target@1` (what it accepts + which configure dialog) and `hook@1` (draggable action descriptor), open registries so any plugin/app can add targets and hooks without kernel changes. Phone: long-press to pick up, drag with edge auto-scroll, drop zones highlight.
- **Banners:** only add the banner drop target through the generic contract. Do NOT merge or rewrite banner-pack (#251), banner-editor (#254) or banners-one work; Brett is reviewing those himself. Note any overlap in the report.
- Rules: add to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar: per-toolbar settings + editor via its context menu, tap-to-confirm on touch only, accepts dropped hooks.' Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.
- Split into clear steps in the store; tests for drop targets/dialogs/move-copy/undo, phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review items.

# Build: claude-settings (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a plugin called Claude. Claude settings. A setting to enable your no-wait in that. A whole bunch of settings that are for Claude, that you check on axHub and then act accordingly." Assigned agent: **Janitor Joey** (book on his card; AXF_AGENT=janitor-joey if supported). Register in Urgent (id `claude-settings`) + banner entry.

## Plugin
Console plugin **Claude** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Claude, context-menu hook 'Claude settings' everywhere). Settings are stored on axHub (shared `_data/claude/settings.json` or a hub settings namespace) so every Claude session (voice, chat, Claude Code, headless agents) reads the same values.

## Settings (grouped, framework settings renderer with the level toolbar)
- **No wait** (owner-only): when ON, Amber's held calls run immediately instead of the 90 s veto / approval. Implement as a standing axHub pass that the console creates on Brett's signed-in click (reuse pass-all / `axhub.pass_grant` machinery, scope all, `include_irreversible` false by default with its own separate switch 'Include irreversible' also owner-only). Options: duration (1 h / 4 h / until I turn it off), auto-off at night. Banner chip while on. Turning it off revokes the pass instantly.
- **Follow Amber** (link to / share state with the follow-amber build's switch; don't duplicate it - read the same setting).
- **Builds:** default model (Opus/Fable/split), launch builds without asking (on/off), max parallel builds, per-build budget cap and daily budget cap (stop + notify when hit), always assign a named agent (locked on), UI Review gate (on).
- **Verification:** trust live store by default, verify only on conflict (current rule) vs always verify.
- **Talking:** persona on/off, tone level, address terms, swearing level, response length (short/normal/detailed), say costs out loud, read build reports aloud vs summary.
- **Notifications:** push on build done / blocked / approval waiting, quiet hours.
- **Memory/notes:** save session notes to Notes Vault automatically, handoff note at end of session.
- Open registry so new Claude settings can be added as data without code changes.

## Claude reads them
- MCP tools via axf-console (and axHub builtin if simpler): `claude_settings_get` (policy ALLOW, read-only) returning all values with plain descriptions; `claude_settings_set` for NON-owner settings only (veto policy). Owner-only settings (No wait, Include irreversible, approvals, budget caps raising) can ONLY be changed by Brett's signed-in console click - agents/sessions can never change them (test enforces).
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md (top): 'At session start and before acting, read Claude settings (claude_settings_get) and follow them.'

# Build: smart-menus (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a dynamic context menu that draws itself depending on where it is and what it's doing. Most common / most likely things at the top. It learns and remembers, predicts what I'm most likely gonna want, keeps that at the top." Assigned agent: **Earl the Ear** (book on his card; if busy and the all-rounder router is on main, whoever is free - record who). Register in Urgent (id `smart-menus`) + banner entry.

## Build (framework level: every context menu in every app, existing and future)
- s1 **Context-aware drawing:** the context menu engine builds the menu at open time from: the target under the pointer (element kind, hook@1 / control@1 target, plugin, screen), its state (selected, running, failed, waiting on approval, has PR, etc.), the current screen, device (phone/desktop). Plugins contribute items with `when` conditions (state predicates) so irrelevant items never show; runtime context items stay the contribution path.
- s2 **Learning ranking, zero tokens:** record every pick locally + synced to axHub per user: (context key = target kind + state + screen, item id, time). Rank with frecency (frequency x recency decay) per context, plus time-of-day and 'what I just did' sequence boosts (simple Markov next-action counts). Top section 'Suggested' = top 3-5 predicted items; the rest grouped below in stable order so muscle memory still works. Plain code, NO LLM calls (test fails if the engine imports an LLM client).
- s3 Pinned items always first (from the pending `context-menu-editor` idea: user pins), then Suggested, then the rest; destructive items never auto-promoted to the top.
- s4 Settings (Settings > Menus, and a 'Menu settings' hook in every context menu): learning on/off, number of suggestions, reset learning (per menu / all), show why it's suggested (tiny hint), privacy: data stays on his axHub.
- s5 Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the toolbar build's hook@1/drop-target@1 if on main (don't edit their files). Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get suggestions, reset, pin).
- s6 Tests (ranking math, context keys, when-conditions, reset, destructive never top), phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/smart-menus.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): dynamic SECTIONS, not the whole menu
Don't make the whole menu dynamic. Each context menu keeps its normal fixed items in their fixed order (muscle memory). Add dynamic SECTIONS on top of that:
- A 'Suggested' section at the top (learned/predicted items, 3-5, per s2) - can be turned off.
- A context section (items that only apply to this target/state, per s1 'when' conditions), clearly grouped.
- Pinned items (user pins).
The rest of the menu is static and never reorders. A menu asset declares which dynamic sections it shows and where; the default is Suggested at top + context section, static items below.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): application menus too + 'what we're talking about' goes to the top
- The dynamic sections apply to the **application menu bar** too (every top-level menu: Builds, View, Tools, etc.), not just context menus. Permanent items stay fixed; each menu can declare dynamic sections.
- New dynamic section **'Talking about'** at the top of every menu (app menus + context menus): items relevant to what Brett and Amber (Claude) are currently talking about. Example: open Builds in the app menu while we're discussing the toolbar build -> that build (open it, its PR, its UI Review, its agent, stop it) is at the top.
- How it knows: add MCP tool `console_context` (policy ALLOW, navigation-only, no data change) on axf-console: {topics: [{kind: build|plugin|screen|pr|agent|setting|profile|note, id, label}], ttl_min?}. Amber calls it whenever the conversation moves to something (and console_show / follow-amber can feed it too). The console keeps a short rolling 'current topics' list per user (decays after ~30 min or when replaced), synced live to every open console client.
- Each menu maps topics to its relevant actions via plugins' contributed items with `when` conditions + the control@1 command registry (e.g. a build topic -> Builds menu shows Open build / Open PR / Open UI Review / Agent / Stop). Plain code, zero tokens.
- Settings > Menus: 'Talking about' section on/off, how long topics stay.
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'When the conversation moves to something in the console, call console_context with it.'

## Addendum 3 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): all of it lives in ONE Menus plugin with tons of customization
- Everything in this build (dynamic sections in app menus + context menus, Suggested, Talking about, context section, pins, learning) is controlled by a **Menus plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Menus + a 'Menu settings' hook in every menu's context menu). Removing the plugin falls back to plain static menus.
- **Customization (tokens/assets only, saved per user on axHub, live preview, presets, reset, export/import as a menu-style asset):**
  - Colours: menu background, text, hover/selected, section headers, separators, icons, per-section accent (Suggested / Talking about / Pinned / context), badge colours, shadow, border, blur/glass, opacity.
  - Fonts: family, size, weight, letter spacing, section header style, icon size, density/row height, padding, corner radius, width min/max.
  - Animations: open/close (fade, scale, slide, drop, none), duration + easing, submenu reveal, item stagger, hover effect, highlight pulse for 'Talking about' items, reduced-motion respected.
  - Sections: order, on/off, max items each, labels, icons, collapse/expand, show 'why suggested' hint.
  - Behaviour: learning on/off + reset, topic lifetime, open on hover vs click (desktop), long-press time (phone), keyboard shortcuts.
  - Per-menu overrides (each app menu / context menu can have its own look and sections) from the hook in that menu.
- Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the Toolbars plugin (toolbar-tap-confirm build) through framework APIs - don't edit their files; share the hook@1 / drop-target@1 contract if it's on main.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get/set menu settings, presets, reset learning, topics).

# Build: ui-review-predicted (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): UI Review must show PREDICTED pictures - what a build will probably look like - BEFORE it's built, so he can approve the look before an agent spends money. Assigned agent: **Snap Sully** (book on his card; he's also on ui-review-shots - run after it or build on its storage fix; if the all-rounder router is on main and he's busy, whoever is free - record who). Register in Urgent (id `ui-review-predicted`) + banner entry. Mark the predicted-shots part of pending item `batch-manager` as moved here (pending_change note).

## Build
- s1 Predicted mockups: when a build is launched (or added to the orchestrator/pending list), generate a mockup per screen it will touch from the brief + step list (+ diff so far while running): render real framework components with the current theme/assets and demo data in a headless browser (reuse rebuild-shots / ui-screenshots capture tooling; do NOT build a new capture system). Phone + desktop. If an LLM is needed to turn the brief into a mockup spec, do it ONCE per build at launch with the cheapest capable model and cache it; record the cost on the item.
- s2 UI Review item created at launch with status 'Predicted - approve the look', badge 'Predicted', before = current real screen (from main), after = predicted mockup. Brett can Approve look / Ask changes (comment goes to the build as an addendum before it starts or at the next step) / Reject (build is held, not started).

items.detail:
Brett, Oct 29 2026: "Design a bunch more cards for the console home screen. If plugins with data or dynamic content don't have a card, design one for them from scratch (you decide what to display and how). items.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
items.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

items.title: Session browser: Claude sessions + headless agent runs, live
items.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): a full-blown session browser for regular Claude sessions AND every headless agent run, monitoring in real time. Live grid, collapsible rows like every other grid: agent, build, job, model, status badge (running, done, failed, killed for budget), tokens, dollars, duration, started time; updates live. Expand a row: plain-English rundown of what it built and exactly what changed (item, what was wrong, before/after), taken from real commits and file changes. Tabs: Context (all text that flowed into its context and what it said back), Tools (every command and file edit), Conversation for regular sessions. Watch a running agent live and kill it. Links to PR/commit/file. Sort, search, filter. Built on Session check-in archive + Codebase changes log + the agent-swarm runner's JSON reports and stream logs. Prices everywhere: the row shows the run's exact total cost (from usage). Expanded 'what it did' shows a price next to every line (estimated: tokens of the turns that produced that change, labelled 'est.'). Context tab: cost per turn; Tools tab: cost per command. Totals at the bottom plus a per-model breakdown.

items.title: Framework grid: built-in sort, search, filter + Date and time column
items.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Every grid that lists builds, tasks, asks or anything else is sortable, searchable and filterable, taking little screen. Basic filter attached by default. Tap header sorts, tap again reverses, long-press adds a second sort. One thin row: small search box + filter icon; on phones just a search icon. Filters hidden until used, then small clearable chips. Custom tables move onto the framework grid. Android parity. Per grid: right-click a grid or its header -> Filter -> off/on for this grid; 'All grids...' lists every grid in the app with the right-clicked one scrolled into view and highlighted, a switch per grid; a default switch decides whether new grids get the filter (on). Defaults are decided per grid by the build: on for data grids with many rows or columns (builds, asks, changes, plugins, PRs), off for small lists (settings, keys, short pickers); record the choice and reason per grid. On grids where it is off, hovering the header for a moment shows a tooltip 'Add the filter to this grid?' with Enable (long-press on phones). Framework grid (part of the app, not the filter plugin): every grid that has no date/time column gets an automatic 'Date and time' column (row created / last changed), hidden by default; grids that already show a date/time get nothing. Right-click the header -> Show/Hide 'Date and time'. Web + Android. UPDATE (Brett): build BOTH into the framework grid. Sort/search/filter live in the framework (not the Basic filter plugin); smart per-grid defaults, right-click on/off, All grids list and hover offer all framework features. Date and time column is ensured at first render: if a grid renders without one, the framework adds the hidden column then. New grids get everything automatically. CI check flags any table not built on the framework grid.

items.title: AmberX Audio Output Recorder -> axHub (no mic)
items.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): AmberX plugin that records all audio the phone outputs while it is on, saved to the server on axHub. One switch + quick-settings tile. Playback capture only, NEVER the microphone. Android 10+; system consent prompt each start and a notification while recording. Calls and opt-out apps (DRM) cannot be captured. 30-minute timestamped chunks, each uploaded to axHub; keep the local file until axHub confirms, queue and retry when offline, small local cap. Built on the capture engine from claude/audio-extract (PR #187).

All ticked; nothing missing. Java compiles only in CI.

items.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
items.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. items.title: Tools plugin: the Tools section as its own plugin, with a Tools tab in Patches web
items.detail:
Brett, Oct 22 2026: the Tools section is a plugin of its own, and Claude handoff depends on it.

- New plugin `tools` (plugin@1 + lifecycle): it owns the Tools nav section and the top-level `tools` application menu that tool plugins add to; it provides a capability service (e.g. `axf.tools@1`) that tool plugins require.
- Claude handoff (and any later tool plugin) declares it as a dependency (`requires`) and adds its entries through it instead of creating the section itself.
- For Patches: the Tools plugin adds a **Tools** tab to Patches web's app tab group (next to Console / Pilot / axHub). Patches itself runs the Tools page; it is not the console page in a frame.
- Patches web only for now (Android later).

items.title: Fix: switches and tab buttons dead inside interface tabs
items.detail: Brett Oct 27 2026: Appearance switches in console settings and the layout (interface) buttons at the top do nothing. Cause: AxfRuntime.scoped() gives a scope settings = Object.create(base.settings), so set()/clear()/reload() assign this.values on the scoped object and the shared settings never change (Main tab cannot be reached again from GizmoX Night / AmberX Signature). Fix: scoped settings forward every member except get to the shared registry.

items.title: Share Search: programmable grid toolbar plugin (search/filter bar + 5 buttons + advanced search), attach to grids
items.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): make a plugin with a toolbar of programmable actions for filtering, sorting and searching grids. Toolbar name: Share Search. HELD: Brett said 'send to orchestrator and hold off on build' — don't start until he says.

Asked, in full:
- Toolbar config lives in one of several settings groups inside the plugin's settings interface (Settings → Plugins → Share Search). Set what each toolbar item looks like, how it behaves and what it does.
- At app launch, if the plugin isn't attached to any data (grid), prompt with a dialog to attach it: lists every grid in a grid with expanding rows. Can attach to several; each attachment has its own saved settings, look, style and actions.
- Search bar can be a Filter or a Search (switch in its settings); updates the list in real time on every keystroke.
- Toolbar settings are in a tab list inside the plugin settings: one tab per attachment.
- Quick access: right-click on the toolbar → context menu item opens that toolbar's settings in a dialog.
- The search bar's settings sit in the toolbar settings' Appearance section: a collapsible container with an 'Inherit from shell' switch above it, collapsed by default. When inherit is off the container becomes expandable and shows every individual style token and setting as in the main app's settings.
- Along with the search bar: 5 toolbar buttons configured to manage the grid's view and actions, plus a button that opens an Advanced search & filter dialog.
- Install the plugin on the Console NOT attached to anything, to test the attach prompt dialog.

Design notes (proposed, Brett to confirm at build start): default 5 buttons = Sort (column + direction menu), Quick filter (per-column), Columns (show/hide), Expand/collapse all, Density (compact toggle) + Advanced search button. Toolbar config stored as a toolbar asset per attachment so it's hot-swappable. Plugin rules apply: framework controls only (inherits app style), plugin-lifecycle@1 install/uninstall, builtWith, settings sub-tab of Plugins, snaps never overlaps (Oct 28 rule), context-menu link via rt.addContextItems. Clash check: pending-grid-view (Pending builds grid toolbar) and opus/orchestrator-grid use the same lib-datagrid — build after/with them; Share Search can later attach to those grids. Android twin of the grid-attach seam is a deferred gap (Android hold).

items.title: Approval history with costs: every approval recorded with details + cost, browsable in Console + axHub
items.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Add cost of approval every time something is approved and display costs, as well as all details and history of past approvals browsing. Can you alert when needing approval without stopping and restarting.' Context: he asked whether sending an approval and waiting costs tokens. Answer given: waiting is free, but each retry check re-reads the conversation (mostly cached). The 15 s x10 then 1 min rule costs about 10-15 checks per 5 minutes. HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; history in the Console AND on axHub's approvals page.

Scope:
1) Cost per approval: every approval records the session's token/cost spent while it waited (number of checks, tokens in/out, cached vs not, USD from framework/schemas/model-pricing.json), plus the time it waited and who/what asked (session, surface, machine, build ref, reason title/description, exact call, result).
2) History browser: every past approval with all details and its cost; filter/sort/search, totals per day/build/session. Console = History view in the approvals-banner plugin (framework DataGrid, expanding rows). axHub = same list on its approvals page. Approve stays on the first screen.
3) Alert without stopping/restarting: a hub-side wait (axhub tool, e.g. approvals.wait / long-poll on the confirmation id, up to ~10 min per call) so a session makes ONE call that returns the moment Brett approves. No retry loop and no session restart. The AmberX app push (already shipped, amberx-push) fires when the approval is created. Then update the shared retry rule (15 s x10, then 1 min) to 'one wait call, re-issued only if it times out' — Brett to confirm that rule change at build time.
Work spans MossesX/axHub (wait tool, cost fields, approvals page history) and AXF (approvals-banner History view, cost capture via codebase-changes hooks / session transcript).

items.title: Windows-style Terminal (Claude Code tabs, connections, profiles) + window snap/resize + settings levels toolbar & level editor
items.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): "Add those plus build a powerful terminal plugin that looks and feels and behaves exactly like a Windows program." Asked, in full:
- 'Those' = the four window gaps: resize from every edge/corner (touch too), snapping (no overlap), keep windows on screen, drop a window on another to split.
- Terminal: native Windows look and feel, no Linux feel. Dockable/undockable, draggable, minimizable, snappable window that opens floating by default. Powerful configuration, preferences and customization with an easy interface.
- A toolbar button adds a tab running Claude Code and prompts for one of the available connections (VPS root, specific containers, axHub, console…). Right-click any tab = interface to manage that tab's connection from the available ones. Claude Code tabs get extra customization profiles.
- From now on every settings interface has a default-on, hideable toolbar that picks Simple / Basic / Administrator / Developer; the available settings show in a collapsible container and the rest in another. Administrator shows them all. Levels: Pro becomes Administrator, Advanced becomes Developer (Brett's pick); Administrator shows everything.
- A switch in settings opens a dialog with two columns: left = sortable categorized tree of every setting in the interface, one colour when available to the selected level, another when not; multi-select; toolbar buttons or right-click 'Add to visible'; right tree shows what's on. The settings interface changes live with every selection.

Upgrades the existing console-terminal plugin (one instance per plugin; it already has container/console/VPS/Claude Code tabs, Mosh mode, xterm 5.3). Folds in apply-all-levels-fable s3 (settings-ui@1 levels review). Patches is paused: its baked copy is skipped. Android twins deferred (PORTING.md).

items.title: Feature Matrix plugin: a skip/keep feature matrix for every build, one dataset, hooks in every builds grid, Apply updates status everywhere
items.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai, windows-terminal chat): "Make a plugin to build a feature matrix just like this [the windows-terminal scope list: https://claude.ai/artifact/CwBGQof4NBe4F3dPTczBvS] for every build and put hooks to them in every builds grid in orchestrator, pending, queued, build manager, etc. I need to be able to access its associated matrix from any entry in any grid. All matrix are compiled into 1 dataset that lists each one in expandable rows that open to display its matrix. The grid has column with date added and time cost to build generated by the matrix. When matrix changes an apply button lights up that updates the status across all tables. Nothing is ever removed only set for skip when time comes to build. They can be added removed whenever they never leave the matrix."

Rules from the ask: every build has a matrix (feature items grouped, each with minutes, model Fable/Opus, why); tick = keep, untick = skip; items can be added at any time and are NEVER deleted ("removed" = skip; skipped items stay in the matrix and are skipped when the build runs). One dataset of all matrices, shown as a grid of expandable rows (row = build; columns include date added and the time cost computed from the kept items); a row opens to its matrix. Editing a matrix lights an Apply button; Apply pushes the new totals/skips/status to every table (orchestrator, pending, build queue, build manager, plan…). Every builds grid gets a hook (row button + right-click) that opens that entry's matrix.

Brett's picks: Refactor profile; standalone plugin (builds-one-page removed); built in its own chat thread. Seed: the windows-terminal scope list (23 items, its db doc scope/selection) becomes the first matrix. Overlaps: share-search s1 (grid-attach@1: grid registry) — the hook seam here should be the same registry or forward-compatible with it; basic-filter (running, PR #155) attaches to datasets too.

items.title: Run unless blocked: 2-min countdown → urgent alarm (red banner + loud AmberX ring) → 1-min grace → runs; Block anytime; zero session tokens
items.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Can you send notification that a command is about to be ran and I can intercept it from the banner and block it before axhub tries sending it.' HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; countdown 2 minutes.

Design: a third tool policy next to allow / confirm, e.g. 'veto' (run unless blocked). A session's call returns a job id at once; axHub holds the call for the countdown (default 2 min, per-tool override possible later) and immediately pushes through the AmberX app (rule: all axHub pushes come from AmberX) and shows it in the console's banner (approvals banner or its own) with the reason title, the exact call, a live countdown, Block and Run now. No action = runs at zero. Block = cancelled, never runs, the session sees 'blocked' when it next looks at the job. Sessions never poll during the countdown: they carry on and read the job result once at the end only if they need it, which saves the re-read cost of approval checks. Approvals (confirm) stay for risky calls: deletes and free-form root shell. Brett picks which tools move to veto (proposal: merge-pr, redeploys, container restarts). Every veto call is logged with its outcome (ran / blocked / ran early) in the approvals history (approval-costs build). Related: approval-costs (history, wait call, resume), axhub-github-write.

items.title: axHub runs approved calls itself: hold the call, run on Approve, drop on Reject; sessions send once and never wait
items.detail: Brett Oct 28 2026 14:18-14:20 (claude.ai): send the command to axHub; axHub waits for approval and runs it or not; the session does not wait. Today a confirm call returns confirmation_required and drops the call, so the session must re-send it with the confirmation_id after approval, which is why sessions poll (each check re-reads the whole chat). Change: axHub stores the full call on create; Approve = the hub runs it itself and keeps the result; Reject/expire = dropped. The session gets an approval id at once and moves on; it reads the result once later only if needed. Replaces the polling rule (15 s x10 then 1 min). HELD: queued in Refactor; Brett says go.

# Chat Viewer: every session stored, synced, searchable, exportable as 2-voice audio (Brett, Nov 1 ~3 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Merge origin/main first (other builds are landing).

Brett: store ALL our sessions (claude.ai text + voice chats, Claude Code sessions, headless build sessions) as transcripts in a viewer. When it loads, it checks for updates: new sessions, continued ones, changed ones, and updates the stored copies. Export any session as AUDIO with two separate voices: one for Brett, one for Claude (Amber).

IMPORTANT reality: claude.ai has no API to pull a user's chats, and we must NOT scrape claude.ai with Brett's login/cookies. Supported inputs:
1. Claude data export: Brett downloads it from claude.ai (Settings > Privacy > Export data) and uploads the zip (or conversations.json) in the viewer (phone file picker). Parse it, upsert by conversation uuid, detect new/changed by updated_at + message count/hash, keep versions.
2. Claude Code sessions: auto-sync the JSONL session files from ~/.claude/projects (root and axfbuild) on the VPS on a timer + on viewer load; incremental (byte offset/mtime).
3. Headless build logs (/root/axf-builds/*/*.log, /home/axfbuild/wt-*/*.log) as 'build sessions'.
4. Hub drop folder: Claude chat sessions can push conversations through axHub memory_write into project amberx-axf, area data, path `sessions/claude-ai/<uuid>.json` (schema below); the viewer ingests that folder too. Document the schema and add a line to _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md: when Brett says 'sync my chats', Claude uses recent_chats/read_conversation and writes each new/updated conversation there.

## Store
session@1 schema (framework/schemas + validators): id, source (claude-ai-text|claude-ai-voice|claude-code|headless|hub-drop), title, startedAt, updatedAt, project, messages [{role: user|assistant|tool, text, at, kind (speech|text|tool), toolName?}], hash, version history. Stored on the console data volume (SQLite or JSON files; your call, justify), not in git. Redact secrets (tokens/keys/passwords patterns) on ingest.

## Viewer (console plugin + AmberX entry 'Chats')
- List: framework DataGrid (sort/filter/search, date columns), source badges, 'updated' badge for changed sessions, counts.
- Full-text search across everything (SQLite FTS or similar), jump to the hit.
- Session view: chat bubbles (Brett vs Amber), tool calls collapsible, timestamps, copy/share, export text/markdown.
- 'Check for updates' on load + button: shows new/changed/unchanged counts.

## Audio export
- Export a session (or a range) as an audio file with TWO voices: Brett's voice and Amber's voice (configurable). Use a TTS that runs on this VPS for free by default (e.g. Piper with two different English voices; install into a container or venv, no GPU), with an optional provider setting (OpenAI/ElevenLabs) if a key is saved in the console keys. Skip tool-call noise; read only spoken/text turns; short pause between turns; chapters per hour. Output mp3/ogg stored on the hub, with a player in the viewer and a download link. Long sessions render in the background with progress.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only, phone-first. Tests: export-zip parsing + upsert/new/changed detection, Claude Code JSONL incremental sync, hub-drop ingest, redaction, search, audio render (short sample) with two voices. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle/menu-reach checks. Phone + desktop screenshots to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'Chat viewer - Nov 1' (use demo/redacted sessions in screenshots). Add an install_steps part. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/chat-viewer.md incl. how Brett gets his claude.ai export in.

origin.brief:
# GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/github-app.md: what Brett taps, where things are stored (paths only), what now uses the app.
